core.text: Attack the preferred powered-trolley supply dependency by withholding trolley starts. This is a counterfactual service failure imposed on the plan, not an observed breakdown. Test the account that multi-carrier powered transport is necessary for timely release; that necessity is a proposed account, not an attributed operator belief.

Fresh builder: construct a hand-carrier-only sequence supplying all nine source carriers while preserving twelve correct sealed releases by boundary 13. Keep B1-B3 initially on the rack and B4-B12 at source. Minimize occupied transfer minutes only after complete release succeeds.

Retain whole-minute boundaries; inspection completion precedes unloading and new starts. Rack capacity is five including active inspection; whole loads unload together, blocked unloading occupies transfer labor. Preserve source and inspection order, nonoverlap and uninterrupted work. Hand trips carry one in one minute. Separate clerks cannot substitute. Eleven inspections take one minute, B9 takes two; spare bracket and twelve seals suffice. No extra capacity, bypass, supplies or floor storage.

Probe the builder sequence with the clock and boundary ledger, recording unload identities, correct releases, rack occupancy, waits and both clerks occupied intervals. Thirteen inspection minutes require uninterrupted inspection from 0. A gap, capacity breach or incomplete correct release defeats the proposed survivor; a valid complete hand-only sequence defeats the necessity account.

residue.text: Closest rival: two full trolley loads then one hand trip. Finite-model prediction: twelve releases by 13 with seven occupied transfer minutes. Hand-only survival predicts nine transfer minutes, displacing two additional minutes onto that clerk while saving both charge allowances. Both retain thirteen inspection minutes, including B9 correction. These are calculated predictions, not trials; survival does not establish labor superiority.

B9 packing mark conceals nine brackets; count, correction, recount and completed sealing remain mandatory. Cause is unknown; no additional discrepancies follow. Later request adaptation is unobserved and cannot change fixed demand. No empirical distribution or global optimum proof is supplied. Synthetic-model predictions require a feasible construction and do not establish depot performance.

tension.account_a: Powered-trolley service is necessary to avoid an inspection gap under the deadline.
tension.account_b: Timely eligible arrivals can preserve the release function using permitted hand transport alone.
tension.prediction_a: With trolley starts withheld, inspection must idle and fewer than twelve correct releases finish by 13.
tension.prediction_b: A hand-only sequence sustains uninterrupted inspection: twelve correct releases by 13, nine source unloads and nine occupied transfer minutes.
